experiment: E1 COVERAGE-RECALL audit — the recall axis missing from the E1 grounding critic
motivation: capability_grounding.py measures PRECISION (is every compiled unit backed by source?). It cannot see the inverse failure the exposure eval surfaced: a solvable issue whose fix IS in the skill source but was never compiled into a *selectable* unit, so a per-node selector correctly declines against an incomplete library and the help never reaches the agent. This audit measures that recall.

method.stage1_extract: LLM reads SKILL.md + references ALONE (blind to the compiled units) and enumerates every source-anchored solvable issue (diagnostic / pitfall / precondition / decision), each with a VERBATIM source quote + stage(s) + severity.
method.stage2_map: A second LLM pass, seeing the compiled unit catalog, decides for each issue whether a unit would actually be DELIVERED to a node facing it (semantic match AND stage-eligible AND not avoid_when-excluded). Batched (<=12 issues/call) so each claude call is bounded.
method.stage3_deterministic: No-LLM guards: every issue quote must verify against the real source (drops hallucinated issues -> issues_ungrounded); every claimed covering unit-id must exist in the manifest (drops hallucinated coverage). coverage_rate + gaps computed in code.
method.transport: claude-CLI-only, RAISES on failure (no OpenRouter fallback) so a silent drop can't masquerade as full coverage. Extraction cached; mapping batched.

headline: Both skills UNDER-COMPILE: 6 units captured 30/51 (58.8%) of peft's source-taught solvable issues, 7 units captured only 13/61 (21.3%) of vllm's. Gaps concentrate in explore + debug — the exact stages where the E2 exposure eval showed the selector abstaining.
interlock_with_exposure_eval: The E2 --with-selector pass showed the selector injects ~0.65 units/node and abstains on debug/explore (82.37% exposure reduction). This audit shows that abstention is SUBSTANTIALLY a compilation-recall artifact, not purely wise pruning: there was little debug/explore content to select because the compiler under-produced units for those stages. Exposure-reduction and coverage-recall are in TENSION — a high reduction with low recall is a warning sign, not an unqualified win. Report the two numbers together.
spike018_training_oom_note: The specific spike-018 case (mid-training backward-pass OOM on a 48GB GPU, fix = gradient checkpointing / grad-accum) is at the extreme end: the source carries the fix only as a side-note inside the QLoRA procedure (references/quantization.md gradient_checkpointing_enable), so buried that the issue extractor surfaced only the LOAD-time '<24GB base does not fit -> QLoRA' case (base-model-oom-single-gpu-qlora, marked COVERED). The training-time-OOM-on-adequate-GPU fix was neither a unit NOR a salient extracted issue.
caveats: coverage_rate is STRICT: not every source sentence warrants a standalone unit, and some 'explore' decision-gaps (e.g. use-trl-for-rl-loop) are partially encoded as avoid_when on OTHER units rather than as positive selectable units — the audit counts them as gaps because a selector cannot surface them as positive guidance. Read severity, not just the raw rate.

The extractor + mapper are LLM stages and nondeterministic; the deterministic quote/unit-id guards bound fabrication but not extraction recall itself (a missed issue is invisible). Re-runs will vary the exact counts; the LOW-coverage direction and the explore/debug concentration are the robust claims.

This is 2 builder-made skills on their own source. The remedy is a BUILDER change (compiler chunking/prompt to lift cross-cutting operational knowledge — error traps, decision points, memory hygiene — into units), then a rebuild; NOT hand-authoring units.
